name: Arcturus JP-4 Jetpack
description: A compact hydrogen-fuel jetpack designed for military rapid deployment, now available on the civilian market at prices that ensure only Tier 4-5 residents can afford them. The JP-4 provides 12 minutes of sustained flight — enough to hop between rooftops or bypass traffic entirely. The fuel is expensive, the maintenance is constant, and the failure mode is a three-hundred-meter fall. But for those twelve minutes, you own the sky.
cost: Φ25,000 purchase, Φ200 per fuel cell (one flight)
autonomy: Manual flight with stabilization assist and collision warning
armament: None standard. Military variants have integrated weapon hardpoints.
common_usage: Corporate security rapid response, executive escape systems, extreme recreation, freelancer exfiltration.
story_hooks: A stolen JP-4 runs out of fuel over a Tier 1 district and the crash reveals the rider was carrying something someone wants back
Black-market fuel cells are causing JP-4s to explode mid-flight — someone is poisoning the supply chain
physical_description: The JP-4 is a bulky, angular frame of scuffed titanium alloy and cracked polymer panels, its hydrogen tanks visible through reinforced mesh venting. Soot streaks and corrosion marks the exhaust nozzles; the ignition controls bear worn-smooth grip tape over cracked plastic. A tangle of exposed fuel lines runs beneath patched thermal shielding, and the backplate shows burn scarring from countless hard landings.
